title: FAMtastic campaign scorecard
description: Output of scripts/score-campaign.py --campaign <slug>. Scored ONLY from what is honestly observable today: the real publish state of each drop's provider records in the local Postiz postgres, matched by the compound (campaign_id, content_id) key from posting-schedule.json. This schema deliberately has NO clicks, impressions, conversions, or CTR fields — Postiz's Post table carries no click/impression column and GA4 reporting is not queried for per-utm_content events (see GoogleAnalyticsReportingService.php), so a scorecard claiming those numbers would be fabricating data that does not exist anywhere in this codebase. Where a metric is not honestly available, this schema requires an explicit false/null plus a gap_note explaining why, rather than omitting the field silently.

generated_at.description: UTC timestamp the scorecard was computed, ISO 8601 with Z.

campaign_id.description: posting-schedule.json's campaign_id, the value carried as utm_campaign.

program_id.description: Offer/SKU this campaign sells, copied from posting-schedule.json.

schedule_path.description: Repository-relative path to the posting-schedule.json this scorecard was computed from.

provider.description: Only data source queried for this scorecard. No GA4, no Drupal attribution tables — those are separate, unqueried systems documented in gap_note / attribution_note.

provider_query_note.description: Human-readable note on how the provider was queried (e.g. read-only docker exec psql against postiz-postgres) so a reader can judge staleness/trust.

clicks_conversions_available.description: Always false today. Postiz's Post table has no click/impression column (state, publishDate, content, image, integrationId, organizationId, createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt, error — no click tracking) and GA4 reporting does not request a utm_content dimension or any click/conversion metric. This field exists so a consumer of this file cannot mistake its absence for an oversight.

gap_note.description: Required, non-empty explanation of what this scorecard cannot honestly report and why (clicks, impressions, conversions, CTR, CPC, real-time click-to-publish bridge) so nobody downstream infers those numbers exist.

attribution_note.description: Optional note on the separate, NOT queried by this script, lead/request/revenue join that already works in AttributionService.php + MarketingCommandController.php (locally proven, not yet deployed) — named here so a reader knows it exists without this script fabricating numbers from it.

channels_requested.description: Channel labels this drop's posting-schedule.json entry requested.

channels_missing_provider_record.description: Requested channels for which no matching Postiz provider record id could be resolved from provider_ids.postiz_scheduled_group / postiz_draft_id. Never silently dropped.

records.description: One entry per Postiz Post row actually found for this drop, real state read live from postgres.

found.description: False when the id recorded in posting-schedule.json no longer resolves to a row in Postiz's Post table (e.g. deleted).

state.description: Raw Postiz state value (e.g. DRAFT, QUEUE, PUBLISHED, ERROR) or null if not found.

publish_success_rate.description: published / provider_records_found, rounded to 4 places. Null when provider_records_found is 0 (never reported as 0.0, which would misleadingly read as 100% failure of a measured population).
